fact: Mooziac is an ultra-lightweight, 100% native macOS music player written in pure Swift and AppKit with zero external Swift Package Manager dependencies.
Mooziac is designed as a lightweight, distraction-free alternative to Electron and Chromium wrappers like Spotify and YouTube Music Desktop, living in the macOS menu bar.
Mooziac is free and open-source software licensed under the MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 ThreeTen.
YouTube Music is a trademark of Google LLC. Mooziac is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with, sponsored, or endorsed by Google LLC.
Mooziac requires macOS 13.0 (Ventura) or later, running on both Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4/M5) and Intel (x86_64) Macs.
Mooziac ships as a Universal 2 macOS application containing both arm64 and x86_64 slices compiled and merged via lipo.
Mooziac's official macOS application bundle identifier is app.mooziac.mac.
Mooziac relies exclusively on Apple system frameworks (AppKit, WebKit, AVFoundation, CoreAudio, MediaPlayer, UserNotifications, Carbon, QuartzCore) with no third-party libraries.
Mooziac can be installed via Homebrew by running 'brew install shirkeharsh/tap/mooziac'.
Mooziac installed via Homebrew can be upgraded by running 'brew upgrade --cask mooziac'.
Mooziac is distributed directly via GitHub Releases as 'Mooziac.dmg' and 'Mooziac.zip'.
Because Mooziac is distributed directly outside the Mac App Store and not notarized with an Apple Developer ID ticket, macOS Gatekeeper may display a prompt stating the developer cannot be verified.
To bypass the Gatekeeper warning, users can navigate to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click 'Open Anyway' under the Security section.
Users can clear the macOS quarantine attribute on Mooziac by executing 'xattr -cr /Applications/Mooziac.app' in Terminal.
Upon launch, Mooziac mounts an NSStatusItem in the macOS menu bar, shows a pop-in icon animation, and initializes docked directly beneath the status button.
Mooziac features a built-in UpdateManager that checks the GitHub Releases API (https://api.github.com/repos/shirkeharsh/mooziac/releases/latest) for new versions.
Automatic background update checks are throttled to once every 24 hours (86,400 seconds) using UserDefaults key 'Mooziac_lastUpdateCheckTimestamp'.
Users can trigger a manual update check at any time by right-clicking the Mooziac menu bar icon and selecting 'Check for Updates...' or pressing the 'u' key while the menu is active.
To uninstall Mooziac, quit the application completely and drag '/Applications/Mooziac.app' to the macOS Trash.

To perform a complete removal of all local data, users can delete '~/Library/Application Support/Mooziac/', '~/Library/Caches/Mooziac/', '~/Library/Preferences/app.mooziac.mac.plist', and optionally their local music directory '~/Music/Mooziac/'.
Mooziac streams YouTube Music inside an isolated WKWebView instance configured with custom CSS, ad-skipping scripts, and native DOM bridges.
Mooziac works seamlessly with both free YouTube Music accounts and YouTube Music Premium accounts without requiring a paid subscription.
Mooziac forces high-bitrate audio stream selection in YouTube Music, requesting 256 kbps AAC or 160 kbps Opus formats.
Users sign in to YouTube Music directly inside the app's browser view (360x650 px); credentials and cookies are stored securely in Apple's native WKWebsiteDataStore.
Users can clear their login session and cookies by right-clicking the menu bar icon and selecting 'Reset Login (Fresh Start)', which wipes WKWebsiteDataStore records and reloads the homepage.
Mooziac uses a lightweight Swift client for YouTube Music's internal InnerTube API at https://music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1 using public web client key AIzaSyAO_FJ2SlqU8Q4STEHLGCilw_Y9_11qcW8.
When signed in, YTMClient generates an authenticated SAPISIDHASH header from the SAPISID or __Secure-1PAPISID cookies stored in WKWebsiteDataStore.
To prevent macOS from freezing the WebContent process during track switches, Mooziac injects a silent zero-gain Web Audio AudioContext node that keeps audio output active during transitions.
Mooziac's DOM observer automatically detects ad playing states, triggers ad skip buttons (.ytp-ad-skip-button, etc.), and suppresses ad metadata from appearing on Now Playing cards or Discord RPC.
Mooziac incorporates a dual audio engine: an online WebKit streaming engine and a native AVFoundation lossless audio engine (NativeAudioPlayer).
Mooziac's local audio engine supports MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV, FLAC, ALAC, AIFF, AIF, OGG, and OPUS audio file formats.
Mooziac natively decodes and plays FLAC lossless audio files locally without transcoding or external third-party decoders.
When scanning local audio files, Mooziac extracts track title, artist, album name, duration, and embedded cover artwork using AVURLAsset common metadata.
Users can import audio files into Mooziac via Context Menu > 'Import Audio Files to Location...', which copies selected files into the configured music folder.
Mooziac contains an integrated offline download manager that uses yt-dlp to download, convert audio, and embed metadata and artwork.
Mooziac's download pipeline reports granular progress across three distinct stages: network downloading, audio conversion, and metadata/lyrics tag finalization.
Mooziac automatically fetches and configures the standalone universal macOS yt-dlp binary into '~/Library/Application Support/Mooziac/bin/yt-dlp' with 0755 permissions.
By default, Mooziac stores all downloaded tracks in '~/Music/Mooziac/'.
Users can configure a custom download folder by right-clicking the menu bar icon -> Settings -> 'Select Download Location...', stored in UserDefaults key 'YTM_downloadsFolder'.
Active and queued downloads are persisted in SQLite across app launches so pending downloads resume smoothly upon restart.
If yt-dlp fails due to timeout or missing binary, DownloadManager attempts a native URLSession fallback download before marking the task as failed.
Mooziac's library interface is divided into 4 tabs: Playlists, Liked Songs, Downloads, and History.
Users can import public or unlisted YouTube Music / YouTube playlists by pasting a playlist URL in Menu -> Settings -> 'Import Playlist from Link...' (shortcut 'i').
When signed in to YouTube Music, liking a track in Mooziac (via heart button, keyboard shortcut 'L', or global shortcut) synchronizes directly to the user's YouTube Music account via InnerTube.
Liked songs are stored locally in the SQLite database 'liked_songs' table, enabling offline tracking even when not connected to YouTube Music.
Mooziac tracks played songs in a local SQLite table 'listening_history', recording song title, artist, album, artwork URL, source type (online or local), and timestamp.
Users can clear their entire listening history by selecting 'Clear Listening History' from the status bar context menu, which displays a warning confirmation dialog.
Mooziac captures trackpad events directly by dynamically loading macOS PrivateFramework '/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/MultitouchSupport.framework/MultitouchSupport' via dlopen.
Mooziac does not require macOS Accessibility permissions to process trackpad gestures because it uses low-level Multitouch contact frame callbacks directly.
The trackpad edge volume slider is triggered exclusively along the top 30% of the rightmost edge of the trackpad (distance from right <= 2.5mm or normalized x >= 0.982, and normalized y >= 0.70).
To eliminate accidental touches while typing, the edge volume gesture requires at least 3.0mm of vertical finger travel before volume adjustments engage, then re-anchors to prevent jumps.
The volume slider uses a smooth 160.0mm travel distance for a full 0% to 100% volume transition, clamped to a maximum change of 0.25 per frame.
Mooziac plays macOS mechanical navigation click sounds (AudioServicesPlaySystemSound 1104) and Taptic Engine feedback during gesture triggers.
Double-tapping the bottom-right corner of the trackpad (y <= 0.15) skips to the Next Track, while triple-tapping skips to the Previous Track by default.
Double-tapping the bottom-left corner of the trackpad (x <= 0.005 or dist <= 2.5mm, y <= 0.15) toggles Play/Pause, while triple-tapping toggles the Centered Lyrics HUD by default.

All 4 corner tap triggers (Bottom-Right 2 Taps, Bottom-Right 3 Taps, Bottom-Left 2 Taps, Bottom-Left 3 Taps) can be remapped in settings to 16 distinct actions including seeking, volume, mute, shuffle, and repeat.
Mooziac includes an interactive visual gesture tutorial window (press 't' in Context Menu or open via Settings) rendered in a borderless dark overlay.
Mooziac supports two volume control modes: System Sound (adjusts the Mac's master CoreAudio output device) and Focus Audio / Separate App Sound (adjusts only Mooziac's media volume).

Mooziac includes Loudness Leveling (target -14 LUFS) that normalizes playback volume across songs using track loudnessDb metadata with a 250ms smooth cosine easing curve to prevent sudden volume surges.
Scrolling over the Mooziac menu bar icon adjusts volume: 6 points of trackpad scrolling adjusts volume by 2%, while a discrete mouse wheel notch adjusts volume by 4%.
When headphones or AirPods disconnect, Mooziac's AudioRouteMonitor detects the default CoreAudio output change and automatically pauses playback if 'isAutoPauseOnDisconnectEnabled' is active.

When Mooziac has focus: Spacebar toggles Play/Pause, Left Arrow rewinds 4s (8s on key repeat), Right Arrow advances 4s (8s on key repeat), Up Arrow increases volume by 5%, Down Arrow decreases volume by 5%, and 'L' toggles like status.
Holding Option with Left/Right Arrow jumps 15 seconds, while holding Shift with Left/Right Arrow jumps 30 seconds.

Mooziac registers global macOS hotkeys via native Carbon event handlers for Control+Option (or Cmd+Shift) with Space (Play/Pause), Right Arrow (Next Track), Left Arrow (Previous Track), and 'L' (Like Track).
Seeking within 1.5 seconds of a track's end automatically advances to the next track in the playlist or queue.
Mooziac suppresses Spacebar and arrow key playback hotkeys when typing into search fields, comments, or web input fields inside WKWebView.
Mooziac displays real-time line-by-line synchronized lyrics in a floating, non-intrusive HUD window (CenteredMenuBarLyricsWindowController) centered beneath the macOS menu bar and notch area.

Mooziac fetches lyrics across 5 prioritized tiers: Tier 0 (Local .lrc sidecars and ~/Music/Mooziac), Tier 0.5 (Local cache ~/Library/Caches/Mooziac/Lyrics), Tier 0.8 (Official YouTube Music InnerTube synced lyrics), Tier 1 (LRCLib exact match), Tier 2 (LRCLib title+artist search), Tier 3 (LRCLib title search), and Tier 4 (Plain text / Lyrics.ovh spaced every 4s).
Cached LRC files are verified against the active track title using [ti:...] tags and Jaccard token similarity; corrupted or mismatched lyric files are automatically evicted.
When the lyrics HUD is visible, WebKit and playback observers poll at 4 Hz (every 250ms) to ensure lyric lines synchronize smoothly with zero visual drift.
Mooziac automatically prefetches synced lyrics and track loudness for the next song in the queue before the current song finishes.
The CenteredMenuBarLyricsWindowController also acts as an on-screen display (OSD) overlay for volume adjustments, track change notifications, muting, and mode switches.
Mooziac connects to Discord desktop clients via direct native Unix domain IPC sockets (/tmp/discord-ipc-0 through 9) with zero external Node.js, Python, or Discord SDK dependencies.
Mooziac's registered Discord application client ID is 1537169013174435870.
Discord Rich Presence broadcasts only current song title, artist, album/playlist name, album artwork URL, and start/end playback timestamps; no private account info or history is transmitted.
DiscordRPCManager listens for NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification to automatically detect when Discord opens and re-establish the IPC handshake.
Mooziac provides multiple UI form factors: a compact 360x120 pill docked under the menu bar, a detachable floating Dynamic Island player, and an expanded 360x650 browse view.
Mooziac offers 4 distinct aesthetic themes: Adaptive (Ambient Dark), OLED Dark Mode, Pure Crystal Glass Mode, and Watery Pure Transparent (Liquid Fluid).
In Adaptive (Ambient Dark) mode, Mooziac samples primary and secondary colors in real-time from active album artwork and projects an ambient glowing backdrop.
OLED Dark Mode renders a pure pitch-black (#000000) container with crisp high-contrast white typography, designed for OLED and mini-LED MacBook screens.
Pure Crystal Glass Mode features a translucent frosted glass card with a reinforced 1.2px solid #B3B8B5 perimeter border for high visibility on light wallpapers.

Watery Pure Transparent (Liquid Fluid) theme dynamically adapts to macOS system appearance: frosted glass with dark charcoal typography in Light Mode, and obsidian liquid glass with white typography in Dark Mode.

Mooziac includes 4 selectable timeline track progress styles: Waveform (dynamic 32-bar reactive waves), Neon Glow (glowing liquid capsule), Cyber Dots (pulsing LED matrix), and Minimal Line (precision audio line).
Users can drag the Dynamic Island player away from the menu bar to float anywhere on screen; dragging changes window level from .statusBar to .floating and reveals a 'Dock Back' reset button.
When external displays are connected, disconnected, or reconfigured, DisplayManager automatically clamps floating and docked windows to visible screen bounds with safe margins.
Mooziac features a zero-telemetry architecture: no analytics beacons, no tracking SDKs (Google Analytics, Firebase, Mixpanel, Sentry), and no crash reporters.
All user data (custom playlists, liked tracks, listening history, download metadata) is stored locally in an SQLite3 database in '~/Library/Application Support/Mooziac/'.
Mooziac runs under macOS Hardened Runtime with JIT enabled for WebKit, outbound network access, and audio output enabled, while explicitly disabling audio input (microphone access).

Mooziac creates an IOPMAssertion ('PreventUserIdleSystemSleep') and begins a ProcessInfo user-initiated activity so music playback continues uninterrupted when the display sleeps while the laptop lid is open.
When the MacBook lid is closed or the Mac enters system sleep, Mooziac automatically pauses playback and enforces a paused state upon waking.
When playback is paused, Mooziac allows WebKit rendering engines to enter low-power sleep, keeping idle CPU usage below 0.4%.
Customizable global keyboard shortcut configuration via a preferences UI is an open feature request (GitHub Issue #2) and is not yet implemented in v1.1.8.
Exporting and importing local playlists as .m3u, .m3u8, or .json files is an open feature request (GitHub Issue #3) and is not yet part of the v1.1.8 release.
A custom accent color picker for OLED Dark Mode is an open feature request (GitHub Issue #4) and is not currently available.
Building Mooziac from source requires macOS 13.0 or later, Xcode 15+ (or Command Line Tools), and Swift 5.9+ toolchain.
To build and package Mooziac locally, clone the repo and run './build_app.sh' for debug launch or './build_app.sh --release-only' for universal release binaries and DMG.
Mooziac uses Apple Unified Logging (os.Logger) under subsystem 'app.mooziac.mac' with categories General, Playback, Sync, Download, Database, and Web.
The official Mooziac support portal is hosted at https://mooziac.threeten.site/support.html, accessible directly from the menu bar context menu under 'Help & Support'.

Mooziac was developed solely by Harsh Shirke (@shirkeharsh). Harsh is a software developer and competitive gamer who plays CS:GO (Counter-Strike) and Valorant. He is NOT a musician, music producer, singer, or sound engineer; he created Mooziac purely because he wanted an ultra-lightweight, distraction-free native macOS music player with zero telemetry.
